pipeline.name: Ops Pipeline
pipeline.description: Command-execution pipeline for issues that require running commands on a remote host (benchmarks, migrations, restarts). Routes trigger → specify → executor → done instead of the coder→PR sequence.

tpl_ops_trigger.name: Ops Trigger
tpl_ops_trigger.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <command>set -e
# Validate that the required execution_target extension key is present.
# The engine's 422 guard (apps/engine/src/dap_engine/api/runs.py) already
# rejects execution_commands that is not a list, so we only surface a
# human-readable check here.
TARGET='{{ extensions.execution_target | default("") }}'
if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  echo 'ERROR: extensions.execution_target is required for ops pipelines.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf '<output>{"implementation_notes": "execution_target=%s"}</output>\n' "$TARGET"
</command>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_ops_specify.name: Ops Specify
tpl_ops_specify.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    You are the specify node of an ops pipeline. Your job is to validate and
    enrich the operator-supplied execution intent before the executor runs.

    Inputs available on PipelineState.extensions:
      - execution_target  : string — name of the remote host / Cortex executor node
      - execution_commands: list[str] — shell commands to run, in order
      - execution_env     : dict[str, str] (optional) — extra env vars

    Do the following:
      1. Confirm execution_commands is a non-empty list. If empty, write a
         clear error into implementation_notes and stop (the executor node will
         read it and abort gracefully).
      2. Produce a concise plain-text run-plan in implementation_notes:
           Target : <execution_target>
           Commands:
             1. <cmd1>
             2. <cmd2>
             …
           Env: <key=value pairs, or "(none)">

    Return ONLY in the <output> block:
      implementation_notes: the run-plan string (or error string)
  </task>
  <execution_target>{{ extensions.execution_target }}</execution_target>
  <execution_commands>{{ extensions.execution_commands | tojson }}</execution_commands>
  <execution_env>{{ extensions.execution_env | default({}) | tojson }}</execution_env>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_ops_executor.name: Cortex Executor
tpl_ops_executor.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    Execute the commands listed in execution_commands on the remote host
    identified by execution_target, using execution_env as additional
    environment variables.

    Report the combined stdout/stderr of each command in implementation_notes
    using the format:

      ## Command results — <execution_target>

      ### 1. `<cmd>`
      ```
      <stdout+stderr>
      ```
      Exit code: <N>

      ### 2. …

    If any command exits non-zero, continue running the remaining commands
    (collect all results) but set a top-level "FAILURE" marker at the start
    of implementation_notes so the done node can detect it.

    Return ONLY in the <output> block:
      implementation_notes: the full result report string
  </task>
  <execution_target>{{ extensions.execution_target }}</execution_target>
  <execution_commands>{{ extensions.execution_commands | tojson }}</execution_commands>
  <execution_env>{{ extensions.execution_env | default({}) | tojson }}</execution_env>
  <run_plan>{{ implementation_notes }}</run_plan>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_ops_done.name: Ops Done
tpl_ops_done.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <command>set -e
# Post execution results back to the GitHub issue.
# GITHUB_ISSUE_URL must be set in the engine's env or passed via execution_env.
ISSUE_URL='{{ extensions.execution_env.GITHUB_ISSUE_URL | default("") }}'
RESULTS=$(cat <<'RESULTS_EOF'
{{ implementation_notes }}
RESULTS_EOF
)
if [ -n "$ISSUE_URL" ]; then
  gh issue comment "$ISSUE_URL" --body "$RESULTS"
  printf '<output>{"implementation_notes": "%s"}</output>\n' "$(echo "$RESULTS" | head -1 | jq -Rs .)"
else
  echo 'GITHUB_ISSUE_URL not set — skipping GitHub comment. Results are in implementation_notes.' >&2
  printf '<output>{"implementation_notes": "%s"}</output>\n' "$(echo "$RESULTS" | head -1 | jq -Rs .)"
fi
</command>
</agent_prompt>
